note: No pyramidion of Khufu, Khafre or Menkaure survives, so this is the size of the best preserved royal pyramidion, Amenemhat III's from Dahshur (Cairo JE 35133), 1.40 m high on a base of 1.85 m, whose slope of about 57 degrees is close to the pyramids' own. The limestone one reassembled at the Red Pyramid and the one found in 1993 beside Khufu's satellite pyramid G1-d are of the same order. It is used only for how high on the apex the joint under the capstone is drawn in the as-built render; the capstone takes the pyramid's own slope, so its base follows from this and the angle. Sigma 0.6 m spans the surviving examples.

The height the six temples of the footprint import are drawn to in the as-built state, against tier3.temple.height for what stands. Khafre's valley temple, the best preserved, still stands to its roof over parts of its granite halls, and its outer limestone walls with their batter rose well above that; the mortuary temples were of the same order. Twelve metres is a massing figure for all six, not a claim about any one of them, and the sigma is wide for that reason.

The height of the roofed corridor carried on a causeway in the as-built state, from the causeway's own top. The Old Kingdom causeways at Giza were walled and roofed passages, lit by slits in the roof, whose walls survive only in their lowest courses, so no height is stated anywhere this project has read. Four and a half metres gives a corridor a priest could walk upright with a roof slab over it; the sigma is a third of the value.
